items.title: Chick Corea — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: my mother, Anna, purchased an upright piano at a funeral when I was 4 years old

ctx.x: Yeah. My Dad, Armando, Armando John... I’m Armando Anthony. I like to call myself Armando Antonio, but Antonio is my grandfather’s name. But my dad, Armando, had his own band, Armando Corea and his Orchestra, through the ‘30s—the ‘30s and the early ‘40s. I was born in ‘41. So my first memories with my folks were of my dad coming back from the gig late at night with all his musician friends piling into our little kitchen in our three-room apartment in Chelsea, Massachusetts, and my mother cooking up some great…

that group because were so happy! They were a happy bunch. And those were the musicians. So my dad started taking me to gigs of his. I guess the very first real big thing that happened is that my mother, Anna, purchased an upright piano at a funeral when I was 4 years old, and it showed up in the living room, which was the middle room of this apartment, with a crane on the third floor, coming through the window—because it couldn’t fit up the stairs. I remember that as a kid, this huge... The window was open, and…
Just fooling around. When did you start to study it formally?
